meta.name: Frontend Product Builder Form Workflow Components
meta.description: Canonical components for organizing form sections, summarizing validation failures, presenting form actions, communicating persistence status, collecting deliberate confirmations, managing file-selection workflows, and protecting unsaved changes.

FormSection.name: FormSection
FormSection.description: Canonical composition for a coherent group of related form fields, including heading, purpose, scope, instructions, responsive field layout, section-level state, and optional local actions.
capabilities: Group fields that represent one coherent user task or domain concept.
Provide a visible heading and optional concise section description.
Use fieldset and legend semantics when the grouped controls form one logical choice or related input set.
Arrange fields through approved single-column, two-column, or constrained three-column layouts.
Present section-level loading, read-only, permission, error, warning, or unavailable context.
Expose low-frequency section-specific actions without replacing the form action hierarchy.
Preserve field order and semantic relationships across responsive transformations.

foundation.source: Section, Stack, ContentGrid, native fieldset and legend semantics
foundation.reason: Form sections require explicit grouping semantics, consistent hierarchy, responsive field placement, section-level feedback, spacing ownership, and boundaries around local actions.

standard.intent: Group ordinary related fields in a route, dialog, or application workflow.
prohibitedUse: Grouping unrelated fields only to create visual columns.
Using one section for an entire long form with several distinct tasks.
Creating a card around every small field group.

compact.intent: Group a small number of short fields in a constrained operational region.
prohibitedUse: Long instructions.
High-attention decision workflow.
Large number of fields.
Using density to hide an overly complex form.

review.intent: Group fields used to capture a human review, classification, rationale, or decision.
allowedUse: Human verification of a machine-generated recommendation.
prohibitedUse: Presenting machine output as a completed human decision.
Hiding critical evidence outside the review context.
Mixing decision controls with unrelated entity editing.

sensitive.intent: Group fields whose submission has material operational, security, financial, or authorization impact.
prohibitedUse: Ordinary low-risk data entry.
Using warning styling merely for emphasis.
Executing the sensitive action directly from an individual field.

readOnly.intent: Preserve form context while presenting a coherent section that cannot currently be edited.
allowedUse: User can review but cannot modify.
Calculated values remain visible beside editable sections.
prohibitedUse: Ordinary entity details outside a form.
Using disabled inputs as the default read-only presentation.
Content the user is not authorized to view.

compact.intent: Dense grouping for small operational forms.

default.intent: Ordinary route and dialog form grouping.

slots.name: heading
slots.description: Visible section heading or fieldset legend.
contentRestrictions: Name the coherent task or information group.
Do not use generic headings such as Informações when a more specific label exists.
Heading level follows the surrounding screen hierarchy.

slots.name: description
slots.description: Optional concise explanation of the section purpose, scope, or consequence.
contentRestrictions: Explain only context applying to the complete section.
Field-specific guidance belongs in FieldHelp.
Do not repeat the heading.

slots.name: metadata
slots.description: Optional scope, source, status, ownership, or freshness context.
contentRestrictions: Metadata remains secondary to the form task.
Critical warnings require visible feedback rather than metadata alone.

slots.name: headerActions
slots.description: Optional low-frequency section-specific actions.
contentRestrictions: Actions must apply only to the section.
Primary submission remains in FormActionBar.
Low-frequency utilities move to overflow.

slots.name: feedback
slots.description: Optional section-level warning, error, permission, stale, or unavailable context.
contentRestrictions: Field-level validation remains adjacent to fields.
Form-wide failures belong in FormErrorSummary.
Render feedback at the smallest truthful scope.

slots.name: fields
slots.description: Related form fields in logical reading and submission order.
contentRestrictions: Fields must belong to the same coherent section task.
Visual column placement must not alter semantic order.
Do not place unrelated fields together only to reduce vertical height.

slots.name: supporting
slots.description: Optional section-level supporting content or derived summary.
contentRestrictions: Supporting content must not compete with editable fields.
Large analytical content belongs outside the form section.

slots.name: localActions
slots.description: Optional actions that operate only on the current section.
contentRestrictions: Do not duplicate the complete form submission.
Section reset or generate actions require explicit consequences.
Destructive actions normally require ConfirmationDialog.

slots.name: state
slots.description: Loading, permission, unavailable, or section error state replacing fields when no usable section content exists.
contentRestrictions: Existing usable field values remain visible during non-blocking refresh.
Do not replace the complete form when only one section is affected.

props.name: id
props.description: Stable section identity used for headings, form-error navigation, and analytics-independent DOM relationships.
restrictions: Must remain unique and stable.
Must not expose raw database or DTO paths.

props.name: variant
props.description: Semantic section purpose.
restrictions: Do not choose sensitive or review only for visual emphasis.
ReadOnly must reflect actual workflow state.

props.name: size
props.description: Approved section density.
restrictions: Density must match content complexity and target environment.

props.name: columns
props.description: Maximum approved field-layout columns.
restrictions: Three columns are allowed only for short, related, predictable fields.
Fields collapse before their labels, controls, or errors become unreadable.
Column count must not alter logical DOM order.

props.name: semanticGroup
props.description: Selects ordinary section semantics or a native fieldset and legend relationship.
restrictions: Use fieldset when the controls form one semantic group.
Do not use fieldset only to obtain default styling.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Indicates that section interaction is currently unavailable.
restrictions: The reason must be visible when not obvious.
Do not disable a fieldset only to create read-only presentation.

props.name: readOnly
props.description: Indicates that section values are visible but cannot currently be modified.
restrictions: Child controls must support a coherent read-only model.
The owning form remains authoritative.

props.name: invalid
props.description: Indicates that one or more section values are invalid.
restrictions: Field-level errors remain present.
Invalid section styling must not replace FormErrorSummary.

props.name: loading
props.description: Indicates that authoritative section prerequisites or values are not yet available.
restrictions: Loading one section must not unnecessarily block unrelated sections.
Background refresh preserves usable values.

prohibitedParents: DataTable cell without a dedicated inline-editing workflow
prohibitedChildren: Complete FormActionBar repeated inside every section
spacingOwnership: FormSection owns spacing among heading, description, metadata, feedback, fields, supporting content, and local actions.
The selected field layout owns gaps among direct fields.
Each field owns its own internal label, control, help, and error spacing.
The complete form owns spacing among sibling FormSection components.
composition.surfaceOwnership: FormSection owns no card surface by default. Sensitive or strongly separated sections may use one approved subtle surface, but nested card stacks are prohibited.
rules: Every section represents one coherent task or domain concept.
Field DOM order follows user task order.
Responsive layout does not reorder fields visually or semantically.
Primary form submission remains outside the section.
Field errors remain adjacent to controls.
Section feedback uses the smallest truthful scope.

recipeCompatibility.notes: Primary composition for separating coherent form tasks.
Configuration and sensitive sections require explicit scope, capability, and consequence.
Review controls, human rationale, and final decision belong to a dedicated review section.
Authentication forms normally use one compact coherent section.
Expanded filter panels may use compact sections without becoming a complete route form.

prohibited: Reading form context without an approved adapter.
Determining field layout from DTO shape.

notes: The owning form or route supplies section state, field values, errors, permissions, and actions.
FormSection only composes resolved content.
Section-specific actions receive callbacks from the owning workflow.

responsive.strategy: Collapse field columns according to minimum readable field width while preserving task and DOM order.
responsive.compact: Use one field column. Header actions wrap or move to overflow. Supporting content stacks below fields.
responsive.medium: Use one or two columns according to field length and relationship.
responsive.wide: Use the approved one-, two-, or constrained three-column layout.
responsive.ultrawide: Constrain form reading width and do not add columns merely to consume space.
responsive.overflowPolicy: Labels, controls, help, errors, metadata, and actions wrap without page-level horizontal overflow.
responsive.zoomExpectation: Multi-column sections collapse before controls or field relationships degrade at 125% browser zoom and 200% text scaling.

accessibility.semanticElement: section with a heading or fieldset with legend according to the semanticGroup contract
keyboard: FormSection itself does not add a tab stop.
Fields and local actions follow normal DOM order.
Disabled fieldset semantics are used only when appropriate.
focus: Form-error navigation may focus the section heading or the first invalid field.
Section loading or refresh does not reset focus in unrelated sections.
Responsive changes preserve logical focus order.
announcements: Section-level errors, permissions, stale state, and loading use their canonical feedback semantics.
The section heading provides context when users navigate among fields.
aria: Prefer native fieldset and legend semantics for related controls.
Avoid redundant group roles when native semantics are present.
Associate section feedback with the section only when it meaningfully describes the complete group.
accessibility.colorIndependence: Invalid, read-only, disabled, sensitive, warning, error, and unavailable sections use text and semantics in addition to color.

content.minimum: A visible heading and one related field.
content.typical: Heading, concise description, several related fields, and optional section feedback.
content.maximum: A coherent bounded task. Large forms require several sections or workflow steps.
content.wrapping: Headings, descriptions, metadata, field content, and actions wrap naturally.
content.truncation: Do not truncate section headings, field labels, warnings, or validation content into ambiguity.
content.localization: Support expanded headings, instructions, labels, feedback, and local actions.
content.emptyBehavior: A FormSection without fields or a deliberate section state does not render.
content.technicalContent: DTO groups, database table names, internal schema paths, and permission identifiers are prohibited.

notes: FormSection organizes fields but does not own their values, validation, submission, or server state.
Multi-step forms require route- or feature-owned step orchestration rather than nested FormSection state.

FormErrorSummary.name: FormErrorSummary
FormErrorSummary.description: Canonical form-level error summary that communicates submission, cross-field, conflict, and normalized server failures while linking users to affected fields or required recovery actions.
capabilities: Summarize several field validation errors after an explicit validation event.
Present cross-field constraints that cannot be attributed truthfully to one field.
Communicate normalized submission or business-rule failures.
Expose links or focus actions that move users to affected fields or sections.
Present version conflicts and stale-form conditions without discarding entered values.
Receive focus after failed submission according to the form accessibility policy.
Avoid exposing raw validation, transport, or server implementation details.

foundation.source: InlineAlert, native alert semantics, Button, link and focus contracts
foundation.reason: Form-wide failures require one normalized hierarchy, field navigation, controlled announcement, safe content, focus behavior, and distinction from adjacent field errors.

validation.intent: Summarize field validation errors after submission or another explicit validation event.
allowedUse: User needs a navigable overview of validation problems.
prohibitedUse: Showing a summary while the user has not yet attempted the relevant action.
Replacing adjacent FieldError messages.
Listing untouched optional fields as errors.

crossField.intent: Communicate a constraint involving several fields or a relationship among values.
allowedUse: End date must follow start date.
At least one contact method is required.
Two fields jointly exceed a limit.
prohibitedUse: Error truthfully attributable to one field only.
General server outage.
Permission failure.

submission.intent: Communicate a normalized form submission or business-rule failure that did not produce a successful save.
allowedUse: Mutation failed while values remain available for correction or retry.
prohibitedUse: Raw network error.
Field-specific validation that should be attached to one field.
Successful save.

conflict.intent: Communicate that the current form is based on outdated data or conflicts with a newer authoritative version.
allowedUse: Workflow state changed while the form was open.
Server version no longer matches the loaded version.
prohibitedUse: Ordinary field validation.
Automatically discarding local values.
Displaying raw version hashes.

unavailable.intent: Communicate that a required submission dependency or service is unavailable.
allowedUse: Mandatory verification cannot currently be completed.
Submission cannot continue until a dependency recovers.
prohibitedUse: Invalid field value.
User lacks permission.
Temporary pending state.

compact.intent: Concise error summary inside a small dialog or compact form.

slots.name: title
slots.description: Concise statement describing why the form could not continue.
contentRestrictions: Use task-oriented language.
Avoid generic text such as Ocorreu um erro when a more specific explanation is safe.

slots.name: description
slots.description: Optional safe explanation of impact and required next step.
contentRestrictions: Do not expose stack traces, endpoints, schema paths, or raw server messages.
Do not blame the user.

slots.name: fieldErrors
slots.description: Optional navigable list of affected fields or sections.
contentRestrictions: Use visible field labels rather than field names or schema paths.
Each item must focus or navigate to the relevant field or section.
Adjacent FieldError remains the authoritative correction message.

slots.name: formErrors
slots.description: Optional list of normalized form-wide or cross-field errors.
contentRestrictions: Each error must explain the operational problem.
Do not duplicate identical messages.

slots.name: conflict
slots.description: Optional stale-data or conflict resolution context.
contentRestrictions: Local entered values remain preserved until the user chooses a resolution.
Material differences must remain understandable.

slots.name: reference
slots.description: Optional safe support or correlation reference.
contentRestrictions: Must be safe to copy and share.
Tokens, secrets, stack traces, and database identifiers are prohibited.

slots.name: actions
slots.description: Optional retry, reload, compare, return, or support actions.
contentRestrictions: One dominant recovery action at most.
Actions must explain their effect on entered values.
Do not offer retry when retry cannot change the outcome.

props.name: id
props.description: Stable summary identity used for focus and descriptive relationships.
restrictions: Must remain unique and stable.

props.name: variant
props.description: Operational scope and source of the form failure.
restrictions: The variant must match the normalized failure.
Raw transport status must not directly select presentation.

props.name: size
props.description: Approved summary density.
restrictions: Compact still requires complete error meaning.

props.name: errors
props.description: Normalized user-facing form errors.
restrictions: Every error requires a stable ID and user-facing message.
Field errors use visible field labels and target IDs.
Raw Zod issues, transport errors, and backend payloads are prohibited.

props.name: focusOnMount
props.description: Allows the owning form to request focus when the summary appears after an explicit failed action.
restrictions: Do not focus the summary during ordinary typing.
Use only after user-initiated validation or submission.

props.name: announcement
props.description: Announcement policy for a newly surfaced blocking form summary.
restrictions: Avoid repeated announcements when the error set is unchanged.
Persistent summaries are not continuously live.

props.name: onFieldNavigate
props.description: Callback requesting focus or navigation to an affected field or section.
restrictions: Target IDs must resolve to eligible visible or revealable fields.
The summary does not mutate field values.

prohibitedParents: Toast as the only form-error presentation
spacingOwnership: FormErrorSummary owns spacing among title, description, field-error links, form errors, conflict context, reference, and recovery actions.
The form workflow owns spacing around the summary and its placement relative to sections and actions.
composition.surfaceOwnership: FormErrorSummary owns one semantic danger or warning surface.
rules: Field errors remain adjacent to fields.
The summary provides overview and navigation rather than replacing FieldError.
Raw errors are normalized before rendering.
Recoverable submission failures preserve entered values.
Conflict resolution never silently discards local changes.
The summary receives focus only after an explicit user action according to policy.

recipeCompatibility.notes: Use after failed validation or submission when errors affect several fields or the complete form.
Account and credential errors must follow account-enumeration and security messaging policy.
Business constraints, conflicts, and sensitive submission failures require explicit recovery.
Changed evidence, missing rationale, and decision conflicts must remain explicit.

prohibited: Reading raw form-library errors directly without normalization.

notes: The owning form or mutation adapter supplies normalized errors, visibility policy, conflict context, and recovery callbacks.
The summary may receive focus after an explicit failed action.
Field links may request focus and local scroll to an invalid field.
Retry, compare, reload, and support behavior are supplied externally.

responsive.strategy: Preserve error meaning, field navigation, and recovery actions while stacking all regions in constrained layouts.
responsive.compact: Stack title, errors, reference, and actions. Field links fill the available width.
responsive.medium: Use constrained readable text and wrapping actions.
responsive.wide: Keep the summary aligned with the form reading width.
responsive.ultrawide: Do not stretch error text across the route.
responsive.overflowPolicy: Messages, labels, references, and actions wrap without page-level horizontal overflow.
responsive.zoomExpectation: The complete summary and all field links remain operable at 200% text scaling.

accessibility.semanticElement: alert or focused error-summary region after a user-initiated failed action
keyboard: Field-error links and recovery actions are keyboard operable.
The summary may use tabindex=-1 when programmatic focus is required.
Static error text does not create unnecessary tab stops.
focus: After failed submission, focus may move to the summary or first invalid field according to the form policy.
Activating a field-error link focuses the relevant field.
Hidden sections must be revealed before their field receives focus.
Repeated validation does not cause unnecessary focus loops.
announcements: A newly surfaced blocking summary may use assertive announcement.
Unchanged errors are not repeatedly announced.
Adjacent FieldError messages remain programmatically associated with controls.
aria: Use one deliberate alert or live-region strategy.
Use a visible heading for the summary.
Field-error links require meaningful accessible labels.
Do not expose internal field names through labels.
accessibility.colorIndependence: Validation, submission, conflict, and unavailable meaning use text, semantics, icons, and action labels in addition to color.

content.minimum: A specific summary title and at least one normalized error or recovery explanation.
content.typical: Title, concise description, field-error links, and optional recovery action.
content.maximum: A bounded summary of actionable problems. Full diagnostics belong in authorized support tooling.
content.wrapping: All messages, field labels, references, and actions wrap naturally.
content.truncation: Do not truncate errors, affected field labels, or recovery consequences.
content.localization: Support expanded titles, messages, field labels, counts, references, and actions.
content.emptyBehavior: A summary with no active errors does not render.
content.technicalContent: Raw Zod issues, schema paths, DTO keys, HTTP statuses, stack traces, SQL messages, version hashes, and response payloads are prohibited.

notes: FormErrorSummary does not own form-library error extraction. A form adapter must normalize errors first.
Server field errors should be attached to their fields and may also appear as navigable summary entries after submission.

FormActionBar.name: FormActionBar
FormActionBar.description: Canonical form action hierarchy for primary submission, secondary navigation, destructive actions, pending state, unsaved context, eligibility explanation, and responsive placement.
capabilities: Present one dominant form action.
Present secondary actions such as cancel, return, reset, save draft, or preview.
Separate destructive actions from ordinary submission.
Communicate submission eligibility, pending state, unsaved changes, and persistence status.
Prevent duplicate submission while a mutation is pending.
Support inline, sticky, dialog-footer, and review-decision placements.
Preserve action hierarchy and usable targets across compact layouts.

foundation.reason: Form actions require stable semantic hierarchy, submission-state coordination, duplicate prevention, sticky placement policy, destructive separation, eligibility context, and responsive transformation.

inline.intent: Present form actions at the natural end of a short or moderate form.
allowedUse: Form whose actions remain visible without sticky behavior.
prohibitedUse: Long form where users repeatedly lose access to required actions.
Dialog footer already owned by the dialog foundation.

sticky.intent: Keep actions and persistence context available while navigating a long form.
allowedUse: Form requiring frequent save or decision access.
prohibitedUse: Small forms.
Sticky placement covering fields, errors, or browser controls.
Using sticky behavior without accounting for mobile safe areas.

dialog.intent: Present actions in a modal or nonmodal dialog footer.
prohibitedUse: Route-level form.
Duplicating the dialog foundation footer.
Several unrelated secondary actions.

review.intent: Present explicit human decision actions with status, rationale eligibility, and stale-evidence protection.
prohibitedUse: Treating machine recommendation as the final decision.
Using identical visual weight for contradictory decisions.
Submitting against stale evidence.

sensitive.intent: Present submission for a materially sensitive or consequential configuration.
prohibitedUse: Ordinary save.
Using danger style when the action is not destructive.
Bypassing ConfirmationDialog where policy requires confirmation.

compact.intent: Compact dialog or small-form action hierarchy.

slots.name: status
slots.description: Optional persistence, unsaved, pending, saved, offline, failure, or conflict context.
contentRestrictions: Status must not replace actionable form errors.
Saved status should not remain permanently prominent.
Conflict must block unsafe submission.

slots.name: eligibility
slots.description: Optional explanation of why the primary action is unavailable.
contentRestrictions: Required when the disabled reason is not obvious.
Do not expose capability keys or internal workflow states.
Field validation details remain in fields and FormErrorSummary.

slots.name: secondaryActions
slots.description: Cancel, return, reset, preview, save-draft, or other lower-priority actions.
contentRestrictions: Actions must support the same form workflow.
Low-frequency utilities move to overflow.
Reset requires explicit consequence and may require confirmation.

slots.name: destructiveAction
slots.description: Optional destructive action kept visually and semantically separate from ordinary submission.
contentRestrictions: Use the danger action variant.
The action must name its destructive effect.
Confirmation is required when the action is irreversible or materially consequential.

slots.name: primaryAction
slots.description: One dominant submission, continuation, or final-decision action.
contentRestrictions: One dominant action only.
Use a task-specific label such as Salvar alterações, Enviar para revisão, or Aprovar decisão.
Do not use generic labels such as OK or Continuar when the effect is ambiguous.

slots.name: pendingContext
slots.description: Optional concise explanation of the operation currently executing.
contentRestrictions: Use only when the pending operation may take longer than ordinary button feedback.
Do not promise completion time without an authoritative estimate.

props.name: variant
props.description: Semantic action placement and workflow purpose.
restrictions: Sticky requires a long-form justification.
Review and sensitive variants require corresponding workflow contracts.

props.name: size
props.description: Approved action-bar density.
restrictions: Compact does not reduce targets below the minimum.

props.name: submitting
props.description: Indicates that the primary form mutation is pending.
restrictions: Must prevent duplicate primary submission.
Entered values and current form context remain visible.
Cancellation behavior must be explicitly supported rather than assumed.

props.name: dirty
props.description: Indicates that the form contains unsaved user changes.
restrictions: Derived from the authoritative form-state model.
Must not be inferred only from the primary-action enabled state.

props.name: valid
props.description: Indicates whether the current form satisfies the active validation contract.
restrictions: The disabled-action policy must match the product validation strategy.
Invalid state must not be the only reason shown when permission or conflict also blocks submission.

props.name: canSubmit
props.description: Resolved submission eligibility after validation, permission, workflow, dependency, conflict, and pending-state checks.
restrictions: The shared component does not calculate eligibility.
Backend authorization remains authoritative.

props.name: stickyOffset
props.description: Approved design-token reference for sticky positioning relative to the application shell.
restrictions: Arbitrary pixel values are prohibited.
Required only for sticky placement when shell offset is not inherited.

props.name: onPrimaryAction
props.description: Callback requesting the primary form action.
restrictions: The component does not execute the mutation.
The owning form validates and submits.

props.name: onCancel
props.description: Callback requesting cancellation, return, or close.
restrictions: Dirty forms may require UnsavedChangesGuard or ConfirmationDialog.
Cancellation must not silently discard changes.

spacingOwnership: FormActionBar owns spacing among status, eligibility, secondary actions, destructive action, primary action, and pending context.
The selected placement variant owns its padding, border, background, and sticky behavior.
The form owns spacing before an inline action bar.
composition.surfaceOwnership: Inline action bars normally inherit the form surface. Sticky and dialog variants own one approved footer surface and divider.
rules: One action is visually dominant.
Destructive actions remain separate.
Pending state prevents duplicate submission.
Disabled actions require a visible reason when not obvious.
Dirty cancellation never silently discards changes.
The action bar emits callbacks and does not own mutations.

recipeCompatibility.notes: Canonical primary and secondary form action hierarchy.
Sensitive actions require capability, consequence, confirmation, and audit-aware behavior.
Human decision actions remain separate from machine recommendations and block on stale evidence.
Use a compact action hierarchy with safe pending and error behavior.

prohibited: Reading form context directly without an adapter.

notes: The owning form supplies dirty, valid, submitting, success, failure, and resolved eligibility state.
Mutation state remains feature- or query-owned and is adapted into the action bar.
Confirmation and navigation behavior remain outside the shared component.
Sticky placement participates in local viewport positioning.
Buttons emit action requests.
The owning workflow controls focus after success, failure, or navigation.

responsive.strategy: Preserve primary action visibility, status meaning, and secondary-action access while stacking or moving low-frequency actions to overflow.
responsive.compact: Stack status and eligibility above actions. Primary action normally fills the width. Secondary actions wrap or move to overflow. Respect safe-area insets.
responsive.medium: Status and actions may occupy separate rows. Primary action remains visually dominant.
responsive.wide: Align status to the start and actions to the end when readable.
responsive.ultrawide: Remain constrained to the form width rather than the route width.
responsive.overflowPolicy: Actions wrap or move to overflow. The bar must not create page-level horizontal overflow or cover the final fields.
responsive.zoomExpectation: Sticky and dialog action bars must remain operable at 200% text scaling and 125% browser zoom.

accessibility.semanticElement: form action region or footer associated with the owning form
accessibility.accessibleName: Supplied by the form context when the region requires a label.
keyboard: All actions are keyboard operable.
Disabled actions cannot be activated.
Overflow actions are keyboard operable.
Enter-key submission follows the owning form policy and must not activate an unintended destructive action.
focus: Visible focus remains on every action.
Submitting does not move focus until the workflow resolves.
After validation failure, focus follows FormErrorSummary policy.
After successful navigation, focus follows the destination route policy.
announcements: Pending, saved, failed, offline, and conflict status use FormStatus or canonical feedback behavior.
The primary action label changes only when the operation meaning actually changes.
Duplicate pending announcements are avoided.
aria: Prefer native button disabled semantics where appropriate.
Loading buttons retain an accessible action name and expose pending state.
Do not use aria-disabled without implementing equivalent interaction prevention.
accessibility.colorIndependence: Primary, secondary, destructive, disabled, pending, conflict, and error meaning use labels, structure, semantics, and icons in addition to color.

content.typical: Persistence status, one secondary action, and one primary action.
content.maximum: One primary action, one destructive action, a small set of secondary actions, status, and eligibility context.
content.wrapping: Labels, status, eligibility, and actions wrap according to responsive policy.
content.truncation: Do not truncate primary or destructive action labels into ambiguity.
content.localization: Support expanded action labels, pending labels, eligibility reasons, and status messages.
content.emptyBehavior: A FormActionBar without a primary action is invalid unless the form is explicitly read-only.
content.technicalContent: Mutation names, endpoint paths, capability keys, state-machine codes, and raw form-state identifiers are prohibited.

notes: FormActionBar is not a generic page toolbar.
The form adapter determines whether validation occurs before enabling submission, on submission, or through another approved policy.

FormStatus.name: FormStatus
FormStatus.description: Canonical concise status presentation for unsaved changes, saving, saved state, autosave failure, offline state, restored drafts, and version conflict.
capabilities: Communicate whether the form has unsaved changes.
Communicate pending save or autosave activity.
Communicate authoritative successful persistence.
Communicate save failure without discarding entered values.
Communicate offline or unavailable persistence state.
Communicate stale or conflicting data requiring reconciliation.
Expose a safe retry, details, restore, or conflict-resolution action.
Avoid excessive announcements during frequent autosave activity.

foundation.reason: Form persistence states require explicit semantics, authoritative completion, controlled announcement, timestamp context, retry behavior, and distinction from validation and mutation errors.

clean.intent: Communicate that the current form matches the last authoritative persisted state.
allowedUse: Form returned to the last persisted values.
prohibitedUse: Save is still pending.
Local changes exist.
Last save failed.
Server state changed after load.

unsaved.intent: Communicate that local changes have not yet been persisted.
allowedUse: Pending local draft before autosave debounce.
Changes restored from a local draft but not yet committed.
prohibitedUse: Treating validation failure as the only evidence of unsaved state.
Showing unsaved when values match the persisted baseline.

saving.intent: Communicate that an authoritative save or autosave request is currently pending.
prohibitedUse: Operation is only scheduled but has not begun.
Presenting saving after the request has failed.
Assuming completion from elapsed time.

saved.intent: Communicate backend-confirmed or otherwise authoritative successful persistence.
prohibitedUse: Optimistic local update not yet confirmed.
Machine operation completed but server persistence remains pending.
Showing saved permanently as decorative status.

failed.intent: Communicate that the most recent save attempt failed while preserving local changes.
prohibitedUse: Field validation failure before any save request.
Permission denial requiring PermissionState.
Version conflict requiring conflict variant.

offline.intent: Communicate that persistence is unavailable because network or required connectivity is unavailable.
allowedUse: Local changes remain pending until connectivity returns.
prohibitedUse: Generic server error.
Assuming changes will synchronize unless the product actually supports queued synchronization.

conflict.intent: Communicate that local form data conflicts with a newer authoritative version.
allowedUse: Loaded version no longer matches the server.
prohibitedUse: Ordinary save error.
Silently choosing local or server values.
Rendering raw version identifiers.

restored.intent: Communicate that a local or server draft was restored and may still require review or persistence.
prohibitedUse: Treating restored content as already saved.
Restoring data without informing the user.
Restoring a draft from an incompatible record or user context.

compact.intent: Concise status inside FormActionBar, a dialog footer, or a small form header.

default.intent: Prominent persistence status requiring supporting explanation or actions.

slots.name: icon
slots.description: Optional semantic persistence-state icon.
contentRestrictions: The icon must match the status.
Animation is allowed only for active saving and respects reduced motion.
The icon is not the only source of meaning.

slots.name: label
slots.description: Concise localized persistence-state label.
contentRestrictions: Use wording such as Alterações não salvas, Salvando, Salvo, Falha ao salvar, or Conflito detectado.
Do not expose mutation or form-library state names.

slots.name: description
slots.description: Optional explanation of impact, recovery, or persistence behavior.
contentRestrictions: Required when offline, failed, restored, or conflict behavior is not obvious.
Do not promise background synchronization unless the feature supports it.

slots.name: timestamp
slots.description: Optional authoritative last-saved or last-attempt timestamp.
contentRestrictions: Saved timestamp must represent authoritative persistence.
Use localized absolute time when audit or review context requires it.

slots.name: details
slots.description: Optional concise supporting context such as draft source or conflict scope.
contentRestrictions: Raw version hashes and storage keys are prohibited.
Detailed differences belong in a conflict-comparison component.

slots.name: action
slots.description: Optional retry, review conflict, restore, discard draft, or view-details action.
contentRestrictions: Actions must explain their effect on local values.
Discarding a draft may require confirmation.
Retry must not create duplicate concurrent save requests.

props.name: status
props.type: clean | unsaved | saving | saved | failed | offline | conflict | restored
props.description: Resolved authoritative form-persistence state.
restrictions: The component does not derive status from arbitrary form-state combinations.
Saved requires authoritative confirmation.
Conflict requires an actual version or state conflict.

props.name: size
props.description: Approved status presentation scale.
restrictions: Compact must retain explicit offline, failure, or conflict meaning.

props.name: lastSavedAt
props.description: Authoritative machine-readable timestamp of the last successful persistence.
restrictions: Must not represent the beginning of a request.
Use an unambiguous temporal format.
Null means no successful persistence timestamp is available.

props.name: lastAttemptAt
props.description: Optional timestamp of the most recent save attempt.
restrictions: Must remain distinct from lastSavedAt.
Useful only when failure or retry context benefits from it.

props.name: announcement
props.description: Announcement policy for meaningful persistence-state changes.
restrictions: Frequent autosave cycles must not create excessive announcements.
Conflict and failure may require stronger announcement than routine saved state.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Callback requesting a safe save retry.
restrictions: Available only when retry is eligible.
The component does not execute the mutation.

props.name: onResolveConflict
props.description: Callback requesting the owning workflow's conflict-resolution experience.
restrictions: Must preserve local values until the user chooses a resolution.
The component does not decide which version wins.

prohibitedParents: Tooltip as the only persistence feedback
spacingOwnership: FormStatus owns spacing among icon, label, description, timestamp, details, and actions.
The containing FormActionBar or form header owns spacing around the complete status.
composition.surfaceOwnership: Compact FormStatus normally owns no separate surface. Failure, offline, restored, and conflict presentations may use one approved semantic surface when displayed at default size.
rules: Unsaved, saving, saved, failed, offline, conflict, and restored remain distinct.
Saved requires authoritative confirmation.
Failure preserves local values.
Conflict never silently chooses a version.
Routine autosave announcements remain restrained.
The component emits recovery callbacks and does not persist data.

recipeCompatibility.notes: Use when dirty state, manual save, autosave, draft restoration, or conflict affects the workflow.
Configuration persistence and conflict status must remain explicit.
Draft decisions, saving, stale evidence, and conflict must remain distinct.
Use only when the authentication workflow persists recoverable configuration or draft state.

notes: The owning form, mutation adapter, autosave controller, or draft manager supplies the normalized persistence status.
The component receives authoritative timestamps and recovery callbacks.
Retry, conflict resolution, restore, discard, and details callbacks are supplied externally.

responsive.strategy: Preserve status meaning and recovery action while wrapping timestamp and supporting details.
responsive.compact: Show concise label and essential action. Description and timestamp wrap below when necessary.
responsive.medium: Allow label, timestamp, and action to share one or two rows.
responsive.wide: Use compact inline status inside FormActionBar or expanded status in the form header.
responsive.ultrawide: Remain constrained to the form context.
responsive.overflowPolicy: Labels, dates, details, and actions wrap. Raw identifiers are not displayed.
responsive.zoomExpectation: Status, timestamp, and recovery actions remain understandable and operable at 200% text scaling.

accessibility.semanticElement: status region for meaningful persistence changes or static text for stable state
keyboard: Static status is not focusable.
Retry, conflict, restore, discard, and details actions are keyboard operable.
focus: Routine status changes do not move focus.
Conflict-resolution actions open or navigate according to the owning workflow.
Retry does not unexpectedly reset field focus.
announcements: Saving may be announced once when a user explicitly requests save.
Saved may be announced politely without repeating on every autosave cycle.
Failure, offline, and conflict are announced when they materially affect the workflow.
Unchanged status is not repeatedly announced.
aria: Use one deliberate status or live-region strategy.
Animated saving icons expose equivalent text.
Decorative icons are hidden from assistive technology.
Time values use machine-readable datetime where applicable.
accessibility.colorIndependence: Clean, unsaved, saving, saved, failed, offline, conflict, and restored meaning use text, semantics, icons, and actions in addition to color.

content.typical: State label, optional last-saved time, and conditional recovery action.
content.maximum: A concise persistence summary. Detailed conflict comparison or diagnostics belong elsewhere.
content.wrapping: Labels, descriptions, timestamps, details, and actions wrap naturally.
content.truncation: Do not truncate failure, offline, conflict, or recovery meaning.
content.localization: Support expanded state labels, relative and absolute dates, descriptions, and actions.
content.emptyBehavior: A clean status may be omitted when persistence context is not operationally useful.
content.technicalContent: Mutation keys, storage keys, query-state names, version hashes, transport errors, and internal autosave identifiers are prohibited.

notes: FormStatus is not a toast notification.
The autosave controller determines debounce, cancellation, queueing, retries, and authoritative persistence.

ConfirmationField.name: ConfirmationField
ConfirmationField.description: Canonical deliberate-verification field requiring the user to enter a known safe phrase, entity name, or nonsecret identifier before a consequential form action becomes eligible.
capabilities: Collect an explicit typed verification value before a consequential action.
Present the expected safe confirmation value visibly and accessibly.
Support exact phrase, entity-name, and safe-identifier verification.
Communicate unmatched, matched, disabled, read-only, pending, and invalid states.
Keep confirmation verification separate from the consequential mutation.
Preserve entered confirmation content through recoverable validation failures.
Prevent typed confirmation from being confused with authentication, consent, or CAPTCHA.

foundation.reason: Consequential typed confirmation requires visible expected-value context, form-owned comparison, normalization policy, accessible validation, and strict separation from the resulting mutation.

exactPhrase.intent: Require entry of a short, localized, explicitly displayed phrase.
allowedUse: Confirm understanding of a consequential workflow transition.
prohibitedUse: Using a hidden or undisclosed expected phrase.
Using a long sentence that is difficult to reproduce.
Replacing informed consent.
Replacing reauthentication.

entityName.intent: Require entry of the visible name of the entity affected by the operation.
prohibitedUse: Entity name is not unique or not clearly visible.
Expected value contains undisclosed normalization.
The entity name contains secret information.

identifier.intent: Require entry of a safe, user-visible, nonsecret identifier.
allowedUse: Confirm the final characters of a safe operational reference.
prohibitedUse: Passwords.
Authentication secrets.
API keys.
Access tokens.
Private keys.
Sensitive personal identifiers unless explicitly approved by product and privacy policy.

compact.intent: Typed confirmation inside a bounded dialog.

comfortable.intent: High-attention confirmation with visible consequences and target summary.

slots.name: label
slots.description: Visible field label identifying the required verification.
contentRestrictions: Use direct task-oriented language.
Do not use placeholder text as the only label.
Do not imply that entering the value executes the action.

slots.name: consequence
slots.description: Visible explanation of the operation that will become eligible after verification.
contentRestrictions: Name the affected entity and consequence.
State whether the operation is irreversible.
Material consequences must not be tooltip-only.

slots.name: expectedValue
slots.description: Visible safe phrase, entity name, or identifier the user must reproduce.
contentRestrictions: The expected value must be safe to display.
Secrets and credentials are prohibited.
The expected value must be selectable and readable.
Do not obscure case-sensitivity or whitespace rules.

slots.name: control
slots.description: Text input receiving the user's confirmation value.
contentRestrictions: The value remains controlled by the owning form.
The control does not execute the consequential action.
Paste remains allowed unless an explicit product security requirement documents otherwise.

slots.name: help
slots.description: Optional explanation of comparison rules or action eligibility.
contentRestrictions: Explain case, whitespace, or formatting behavior when relevant.
Do not reveal secret validation details.

slots.name: matchStatus
slots.description: Optional concise indication that the confirmation currently matches.
contentRestrictions: Success indicates only that the verification input matches.
Success must not imply that the consequential mutation has completed.

slots.name: error
slots.description: Current normalized confirmation validation error.
contentRestrictions: Explain that the value does not match or that confirmation is required.
Do not expose comparison implementation details.

props.name: id
props.description: Stable confirmation-field identity.
restrictions: Must be unique and stable.

props.name: name
props.description: Stable form-field name.
restrictions: Maps to one confirmation input value.

props.name: variant
props.description: Semantic confirmation-value source.
restrictions: The selected variant must match the displayed expected value.
Identifier must remain safe and nonsecret.

props.name: size
props.description: Approved confirmation-field density.
restrictions: High-impact consequences should not use density that obscures context.

props.name: value
props.description: Controlled confirmation input.
restrictions: Entered content must remain available through recoverable validation failures.
Do not persist the value independently of the owning workflow.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Controlled input-change callback.
restrictions: The callback updates form state only.
It must not execute the consequential operation.

props.name: expectedDisplayValue
props.description: Safe visible value the user is asked to reproduce.
restrictions: Must be safe to display.
Must match the form validation contract.
Must not contain a password, token, private key, or authentication secret.

props.name: matched
props.description: Form-owned result of comparing the entered value with the approved expected value.
restrictions: The shared component does not determine business eligibility from this value alone.
Matched enables only the next workflow condition and does not imply successful mutation.

props.name: comparisonMode
props.description: Documented normalization contract used by the owning validation schema.
restrictions: The visible instructions must match the selected comparison mode.
Do not apply undocumented Unicode, punctuation, or identifier normalization.

props.name: required
props.description: Indicates that successful confirmation is required for the workflow.
restrictions: Must remain synchronized with form validation.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Indicates that confirmation cannot currently be entered.
restrictions: The reason must be visible when not obvious.

props.name: invalid
props.description: Indicates that the current confirmation input fails the active contract.
restrictions: Requires an associated normalized FieldError.

spacingOwnership: ConfirmationField owns spacing among label, consequence, expected value, control, help, match status, and error.
The parent workflow owns spacing around the complete field and the consequential action.
composition.surfaceOwnership: ConfirmationField owns no independent outer card. The parent sensitive section or dialog owns the warning surface.
rules: Typed confirmation is used only when additional deliberate friction is justified.
The expected value remains visible and safe.
Comparison remains synchronized with the form schema.
Matching does not execute the operation.
Authentication and reauthentication require dedicated authentication workflows.
Consent uses CheckboxField rather than typed confirmation by default.

recipeCompatibility.notes: Use only for consequential operations requiring deliberate typed verification.
Tenant, security, identity, and destructive administration may require typed confirmation.
Use only when policy requires additional verification beyond decision and rationale.
Typed confirmation does not replace credential entry, MFA, or reauthentication.

notes: The owning form controls value, comparison result, validation, dirty state, and submission eligibility.
The feature supplies the safe expected value and consequential-action context.
The field emits input changes only.
Selecting or copying the visible expected value remains ordinary browser behavior.

responsive.strategy: Preserve the complete consequence, expected value, input, and validation context in one readable vertical sequence.
responsive.compact: Stack all content. The input fills the available width. Long expected values wrap or use safe code wrapping.
responsive.medium: Use the form reading width and keep the expected value near the input.
responsive.wide: Constrain the confirmation region rather than stretching across the route.
responsive.ultrawide: Do not increase friction or content merely because additional width exists.
responsive.overflowPolicy: Expected values, consequences, help, and errors wrap without page-level overflow.
responsive.zoomExpectation: The expected value and input remain readable and operable at 200% text scaling.

accessibility.semanticElement: labeled text input within a consequential-action form region
keyboard: The input uses native text-editing behavior.
Paste remains available unless an approved requirement documents otherwise.
The field does not submit the form automatically when the value matches.
focus: The input has a visible focus indicator.
Validation does not clear or blur the input.
After a failed consequential action, focus follows FormErrorSummary policy.
announcements: Help and errors are associated with the input.
A newly matched state may be exposed without excessive live announcements.
Matching does not announce that the consequential action succeeded.
aria: Use aria-describedby for consequence, expected value, help, and error where appropriate.
Use aria-invalid when invalid.
Do not use password semantics for visible confirmation values.
accessibility.colorIndependence: Matched, unmatched, invalid, disabled, and unavailable states use text and semantics in addition to color.

content.minimum: Visible consequence, safe expected value, labeled input, and verification contract.
content.typical: Warning context, entity name or phrase, input, help, and conditional error.
content.maximum: One short safe confirmation value. Complex approvals require structured review controls.
content.wrapping: Consequence, expected value, help, and errors wrap naturally.
content.truncation: The expected value must not be truncated into ambiguity.
content.localization: Support localized labels, phrases, consequences, instructions, and validation messages.
content.emptyBehavior: A ConfirmationField without a safe expected value is invalid.
content.technicalContent: Passwords, tokens, secrets, private identifiers, raw database IDs, capability keys, and mutation names are prohibited.

notes: ConfirmationField adds deliberate verification but is not a security boundary.
Backend authorization, validation, idempotency, and operation safety remain authoritative.

FileUpload.name: FileUpload
FileUpload.description: Canonical file-selection and upload-status composition for selecting, reviewing, validating, removing, retrying, and monitoring files while transport and security processing remain feature-owned.
capabilities: Select files through a native file picker.
Support optional drag-and-drop without making drag-and-drop the only interaction.
Present single-file and multiple-file workflows.
Present document, image, and evidence-oriented upload variants.
Communicate selected, queued, uploading, processing, completed, failed, rejected, and unavailable file states.
Expose normalized file name, size, type, progress, security-processing, and error context.
Allow removal, cancellation, and retry when the owning upload workflow supports them.
Preserve accessibility and keyboard operation without requiring pointer gestures.
Keep upload transport, storage, virus scanning, and server validation outside the visual component.

foundation.source: Native file input, Button, Progress, StatusBadge, FieldHelp, FieldError
foundation.reason: File workflows require accessible selection, per-file state, cancellation and retry policy, security-processing context, safe preview boundaries, and strict separation from transport implementation.

single.intent: Select and manage one file value.
prohibitedUse: Several evidence files.
Silently replacing an existing file without confirmation or clear state.
Using one input for several semantically different document requirements.

multiple.intent: Select and manage a bounded collection of files with independent states.
prohibitedUse: Unbounded uploads.
Folder synchronization.
Large media-library management.
Using one upload area for unrelated document categories without visible classification.

image.intent: Select one or more image files with an approved safe preview and image-specific guidance.
prohibitedUse: Previewing untrusted SVG or active content without sanitization policy.
Treating the client preview as evidence of successful upload.
Performing image transformation silently.

evidence.intent: Collect review or audit evidence with explicit source, category, security-processing, and completion context.
prohibitedUse: Treating an uploaded file as trusted evidence before required scanning or processing completes.
Allowing evidence submission without required provenance.
Hiding failed or rejected files.

compact.intent: Compact single-file or small attachment selector.

slots.name: label
slots.description: Visible upload-field label.
contentRestrictions: Name the document or attachment purpose.
Do not use generic File when the required artifact is known.
Placeholder content does not replace the label.

slots.name: instructions
slots.description: Persistent accepted-type, size, count, security, and purpose guidance.
contentRestrictions: State accepted formats in user-facing terms.
State maximum count and file size.
Explain security processing or delayed availability when applicable.
Client restrictions must not be described as complete security validation.

slots.name: selectionControl
slots.description: Native file input and visible picker action.
contentRestrictions: The native input must remain operable and correctly labeled.
The button opens the file picker only.
Selection does not imply upload completion.

slots.name: dropzone
slots.description: Optional pointer drag-and-drop target sharing the same selection contract.
contentRestrictions: Drag-and-drop is supplementary.
Keyboard and touch users must have an equivalent picker action.
The complete page must not become a drop target.

slots.name: fileItem
slots.description: One normalized selected or uploaded file record.
contentRestrictions: Every file requires stable identity.
Do not use array index as identity for mutable upload collections.
Do not render raw File objects or transport responses.

slots.name: preview
slots.description: Optional approved safe preview.
contentRestrictions: Preview does not indicate successful upload or safe processing.
Object URLs must be revoked when no longer needed.
Untrusted active content must not execute.
Preview alt text must reflect the file's purpose.

slots.name: fileMetadata
slots.description: File name, size, type, source, and optional upload timestamp.
contentRestrictions: File names must be safely rendered as text.
Use localized file sizes.
Do not expose temporary storage keys or signed URLs.

slots.name: progress
slots.description: Optional determinate or indeterminate per-file upload progress.
contentRestrictions: Determinate progress requires authoritative progress data.
Do not fabricate percentages.
Processing after transport completion remains a separate state.

slots.name: status
slots.description: Per-file selected, queued, uploading, processing, completed, failed, rejected, or unavailable status.
contentRestrictions: Uploaded and processed remain distinct.
Completed requires authoritative confirmation.
Rejected files remain visible until the user removes or replaces them.

slots.name: fileActions
slots.description: Optional remove, cancel, retry, replace, download, or open actions.
contentRestrictions: Actions must match the current file state.
Retry must not start duplicate uploads.
Remove must explain whether it removes a local selection or a persisted attachment.
Download and open require authorized safe URLs supplied externally.

slots.name: aggregateStatus
slots.description: Optional collection-level count, progress, warning, or failure summary.
contentRestrictions: Do not hide individual failed files behind an aggregate success.
Unknown totals remain unknown.

slots.name: error
slots.description: Normalized field-level or file-level validation and upload errors.
contentRestrictions: Distinguish selection validation, upload transport failure, processing rejection, and permission failure.
Do not expose raw storage, scanner, or HTTP errors.

props.name: id
props.description: Stable upload-field identity.
restrictions: Must remain unique and stable.

props.name: name
props.description: Stable form-field name.
restrictions: Maps to one file or one bounded file collection.

props.name: variant
props.description: Semantic file workflow.
restrictions: Evidence requires provenance and security-processing policy.
Image requires an approved preview policy.

props.name: size
props.description: Approved upload-field density.
restrictions: Compact must preserve usable picker and file actions.

props.name: files
props.description: Controlled normalized selected and uploaded file records.
restrictions: Every item requires a stable ID, safe display name, size, normalized type, and status.
Do not pass raw transport responses into the visual component.
Raw File objects may be supplied only through selection callbacks and remain owned by the feature.

props.name: multiple
props.description: Allows selection of more than one file.
restrictions: Must match the variant and form value model.
Maximum count remains explicit.

props.name: accept
props.description: User-facing and native-picker accepted type hints.
restrictions: Accept is not a security boundary.
Server-side validation remains mandatory.
MIME type and extension policies must be documented together.

props.name: maximumFiles
props.description: Maximum number of files allowed by the form contract.
restrictions: Must be one or greater.
Must match server and workflow constraints.

props.name: maximumFileSizeBytes
props.description: Maximum size of one file according to the authoritative contract.
restrictions: Must match server validation.
Client checks improve feedback but do not replace server enforcement.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables selection and state-changing file actions.
restrictions: Existing file context remains visible.
The reason must be available when not obvious.

props.name: required
props.description: Indicates that one or more valid completed files are required.
restrictions: Must define whether selected, uploaded, processed, or completed satisfies the requirement.
Must remain synchronized with form and server validation.

props.name: invalid
props.description: Indicates that the current file collection fails the form contract.
restrictions: Requires normalized field or file errors.
One rejected file must not necessarily invalidate successfully completed files unless the workflow requires it.

props.name: dragAndDrop
props.description: Enables supplementary pointer drag-and-drop interaction.
restrictions: Native picker interaction remains available.
Drag-and-drop must not be required.

props.name: onFilesSelected
props.description: Emits newly selected browser File objects to the owning feature.
restrictions: The shared component does not upload the files.
The feature validates, normalizes, fingerprints, queues, and transports them.

props.name: onRemoveFile
props.description: Requests removal of one selected or uploaded file.
restrictions: The owning feature decides whether confirmation or server deletion is required.

props.name: onCancelFile
props.description: Requests cancellation of an eligible pending upload.
restrictions: Cancellation availability must match the transport adapter.

props.name: onRetryFile
props.description: Requests retry of one failed eligible file.
restrictions: Retry must use the owning workflow's idempotency and duplicate-prevention policy.

prohibitedParents: DataTable cell without an attachment-editing workflow
spacingOwnership: FileUpload owns spacing among label, instructions, selection controls, dropzone, file items, progress, status, actions, aggregate status, and errors.
Each UploadFileItem owns spacing among preview, name, metadata, progress, status, and actions.
The parent FormSection owns spacing around the complete upload field.
composition.surfaceOwnership: FileUpload owns one selection surface and one bounded item surface per file. Nested cards around each item region are prohibited.
rules: File selection and file transport remain separate.
Drag-and-drop is supplementary.
Client validation is not a security boundary.
Per-file states remain visible.
Uploaded and processed remain distinct.
Completed requires authoritative confirmation.
Unsafe previews are prohibited.
The component does not execute upload, storage, deletion, or download requests.

recipeCompatibility.notes: Use for bounded file values with explicit completion requirements.
Configuration imports, certificates, logos, and documents require explicit security and validation policy.
Evidence uploads require source, category, security-processing, and decision-freshness handling.
Use inside an explicit attachment-editing workflow rather than ordinary read-only entity presentation.
Authentication credentials and identity secrets must not be collected through a generic FileUpload.

notes: The feature owns browser File objects, validation, upload queue, cancellation, retry, progress, transport, security processing, and normalized file items.
The form owns whether the resulting completed file IDs satisfy submission requirements.
The shared component renders controlled resolved state.
The native file picker is a browser-controlled external interaction.
Drag-and-drop events and local preview object URLs remain bounded to the component and feature.
Object URLs must be revoked.
Network and storage side effects remain external.

responsive.strategy: Preserve file purpose, status, progress, errors, and actions while stacking item content before metadata or controls become crowded.
responsive.compact: Use a full-width picker action. Stack preview, file name, metadata, progress, status, and actions. Move low-frequency actions to overflow.
responsive.medium: Use one or two item-content rows according to preview and metadata.
responsive.wide: Align file metadata, progress, status, and actions when readable.
responsive.ultrawide: Constrain upload and item reading width rather than stretching file names across the route.
responsive.overflowPolicy: File names and metadata wrap or use safe middle truncation with full-value access. Upload regions must not cause page-level overflow.
responsive.zoomExpectation: Selection, file states, progress, errors, and actions remain usable at 200% text scaling.

accessibility.semanticElement: labeled native file input with an optional supplementary drop region and semantic file list
keyboard: The file picker is keyboard operable.
Drag-and-drop is never required.
Remove, cancel, retry, replace, open, and download actions are keyboard operable when available.
File items do not become unnecessary composite widgets.
focus: Opening and closing the native picker preserves expected browser focus behavior.
Removing a file moves focus to the next logical item or the selection control.
Retry and status updates do not reset focus.
Validation does not clear eligible selected files automatically.
announcements: Selection count, rejected files, upload failures, and completed states may be announced when user initiated.
Progress updates are throttled and not announced for every percentage change.
Processing and scanning states expose equivalent textual meaning.
aria: Use a native file input.
The dropzone must not replace the native input.
Progress uses appropriate determinate or indeterminate semantics.
Per-file actions require file-specific accessible names.
Use aria-describedby for accepted types, limits, security processing, and errors.
accessibility.colorIndependence: Selected, uploading, processing, completed, failed, rejected, disabled, and unavailable meaning use text, progress, semantics, and icons in addition to color.

content.minimum: Visible label, accepted-file guidance, and accessible native file selection.
content.typical: Picker, optional dropzone, bounded file list, metadata, progress, status, actions, and errors.
content.maximum: A bounded file collection defined by the form contract. Large asset management requires a dedicated route.
content.wrapping: File names, guidance, metadata, statuses, and errors wrap safely.
content.truncation: File names may use safe middle truncation only when the complete name remains accessible.
content.localization: Support localized labels, sizes, file counts, accepted formats, statuses, errors, and actions.
content.emptyBehavior: No selected files use the selection state rather than a generic empty page.
content.technicalContent: Storage keys, signed URLs, scanner payloads, MIME-parser errors, bucket names, stack traces, and raw HTTP errors are prohibited.

notes: FileUpload is not a transport or storage abstraction.
Server-side validation, authorization, scanning, storage, idempotency, retention, and audit remain mandatory.

UnsavedChangesGuard.name: UnsavedChangesGuard
UnsavedChangesGuard.description: Canonical navigation and dismissal guard protecting unsaved form changes during route transitions, dialog closure, context switching, browser unload, and other workflow exits.
capabilities: Detect a resolved active unsaved-change condition supplied by the owning workflow.
Block or pause internal route navigation while changes remain unsaved.
Block dialog or drawer closure when closure would discard changes.
Block entity, tenant, tab, or workflow-context switching when local changes would be lost.
Register browser beforeunload protection when necessary.
Present stay, discard-and-continue, and optional save-and-continue choices.
Continue a blocked transition only after explicit discard or authoritative successful save.
Preserve form values while the guard is displayed.
Prevent duplicate guard dialogs and repeated blocked transitions.

foundation.source: ConfirmationDialog, FormStatus, FormErrorSummary, router blocker adapter, beforeunload adapter
foundation.reason: Unsaved-change protection requires route and dialog integration, controlled blocked-transition state, authoritative save coordination, accessible confirmation, browser limitations, and explicit value-preservation policy.

routeNavigation.intent: Protect unsaved changes before an internal application route transition.
allowedUse: Browser back or forward navigation handled by the router.
prohibitedUse: Blocking navigation when the form is clean.
Executing the destination transition before user resolution.
Losing the original destination during save-and-continue.

dialogClose.intent: Protect unsaved values before closing a dialog, drawer, sheet, or bounded editing surface.
prohibitedUse: Ignoring Escape without explaining why.
Closing the editing surface behind the guard.
Showing two nested confirmation dialogs.

contextSwitch.intent: Protect unsaved values before changing the entity, tenant, record, tab, step, or operational context supplying the form.
allowedUse: Change a workflow step that unmounts the form.
Change a record in a split-view editor.
prohibitedUse: Blocking harmless local tabs that preserve the form.
Discarding local values when context loading fails.
Proceeding to an incompatible context before successful save.

browserUnload.intent: Protect unsaved values during browser refresh, tab closure, external navigation, or document unload.
allowedUse: External link replacing the current document.
prohibitedUse: Depending on custom dialog text controlled by the application.
Guaranteeing that every browser or platform will display the prompt.
Using beforeunload when no unsaved changes exist.

compact.intent: Unsaved-change confirmation for a small dialog or drawer.

default.intent: Route, context-switch, or major editing-workflow guard.

slots.name: title
slots.description: Concise warning that unsaved changes may be lost.
contentRestrictions: Use direct language.
Do not imply that changes were saved.
Do not blame the user.

slots.name: description
slots.description: Visible explanation of the blocked transition and available choices.
contentRestrictions: Explain that leaving or switching will discard local changes.
Explain whether save-before-leaving is available.
State when file selections or in-progress uploads cannot be preserved.

slots.name: changeSummary
slots.description: Optional bounded summary of affected sections, changed fields, files, or workflow state.
contentRestrictions: Use user-facing field and section labels.
Do not expose raw form values containing sensitive information.
Do not list every changed field when a concise summary is sufficient.

slots.name: destination
slots.description: Optional safe description of the destination or context the user attempted to open.
contentRestrictions: Use a user-facing destination label.
Do not expose raw URLs, route IDs, or internal context keys.

slots.name: saveStatus
slots.description: Optional saving, failed, offline, or conflict status while attempting save-and-continue.
contentRestrictions: The guard remains open until authoritative save succeeds or the user chooses another action.
Save failure must preserve the blocked destination and form values.

slots.name: stayAction
slots.description: Action returning focus to the form without discarding changes.
contentRestrictions: This is normally the safest action.
Use a clear label such as Continuar editando.

slots.name: discardAction
slots.description: Explicit action discarding local changes and continuing the blocked transition.
contentRestrictions: Use danger semantics when data loss is material.
Name the consequence, such as Descartar alterações.
Must not be the default Enter action accidentally.

slots.name: saveAndContinueAction
slots.description: Optional action saving the form and continuing only after authoritative success.
contentRestrictions: Render only when save is eligible.
Must prevent duplicate save attempts.
The transition occurs only after authoritative save success.
Validation, permission, conflict, and upload completion remain enforced.

props.name: variant
props.description: Type of exit being protected.
restrictions: The selected variant must match the blocked interaction.
A workflow may compose more than one adapter around the same resolved dirty state.

props.name: size
props.description: Approved guard-dialog density.
restrictions: Compact must preserve explicit data-loss meaning.

props.name: active
props.description: Resolved condition indicating that leaving the current context would discard unsaved changes.
restrictions: Must be false after authoritative save, explicit reset, or deliberate discard.
Must not be derived solely from whether the submit button is enabled.

props.name: open
props.description: Controlled visibility of the application guard dialog.
restrictions: Browser beforeunload prompts remain browser-controlled.
Only one application guard dialog may be active.

props.name: blockedTransition
props.description: Normalized description and continuation handle for the blocked route, close, or context transition.
restrictions: Must not expose raw router internals to presentation.
The destination must remain stable while save is pending.
A new transition must not silently replace an unresolved consequential destination.

props.name: saving
props.description: Indicates that save-and-continue is pending.
restrictions: Must prevent duplicate save requests.
The guard remains open until authoritative resolution.

props.name: canSaveBeforeLeave
props.description: Resolved eligibility for save-and-continue.
restrictions: Must include validation, permission, conflict, upload, dependency, and pending-state checks.
The component does not calculate eligibility.

props.name: beforeUnloadEnabled
props.description: Allows the owning browser adapter to register unload protection while active.
restrictions: Registration occurs only while active.
Custom browser prompt text must not be assumed.
Platform behavior may vary.

props.name: onStay
props.description: Cancels the blocked transition and returns the user to editing.
restrictions: Must preserve form values.
Must restore focus according to the originating interaction.

props.name: onDiscardAndContinue
props.description: Explicitly discards local changes and continues the blocked transition.
restrictions: Must clear the dirty baseline deliberately.
Must continue only the intended blocked transition.
Must not execute without explicit user activation.

props.name: onSaveAndContinue
props.description: Requests save and continues the blocked transition only after authoritative success.
restrictions: The component does not execute the mutation.
The owning workflow preserves the blocked transition through validation and mutation resolution.
Failure leaves the user in the current editing context.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Controlled application-dialog visibility callback.
restrictions: Closing the guard without resolution must behave as stay.
Backdrop and Escape behavior must not discard changes.

spacingOwnership: UnsavedChangesGuard owns spacing within the guard dialog among title, description, change summary, destination, save status, and actions.
The underlying form retains its existing layout and values.
The ConfirmationDialog foundation owns modal padding and action alignment.
composition.surfaceOwnership: UnsavedChangesGuard uses one ConfirmationDialog surface. It must not open an additional nested modal for the same unresolved transition.
rules: The guard activates only when leaving would discard actual unsaved changes.
Values remain preserved while the guard is open.
Closing the guard without resolution means stay.
Discard requires explicit activation.
Save-and-continue waits for authoritative success.
Save failure preserves the destination and local values.
Browser unload behavior remains browser-controlled.
Only one unresolved guard transition exists at a time.

libraries: React Router blocker adapter or approved project router integration

recipeCompatibility.notes: Required when user-entered changes could be lost through route or workflow exit.
Protect scope switching and navigation away from modified configuration.
Protect human rationale and decision changes during evidence or record switching.
Use only for authentication-related configuration containing meaningful unsaved user work.

prohibited: Reading raw router internals in presentation.
Executing navigation without an approved transition adapter.

notes: The form supplies authoritative dirty and save state.
The route or editing-surface adapter owns blocked transitions and continuation.
The browser adapter owns beforeunload registration.
The shared component presents controlled resolution choices.
Internal navigation continuation occurs through the owning blocker adapter.
Browser beforeunload registration is an external browser side effect.
The component does not persist, reset, or mutate form data directly.

responsive.strategy: Preserve data-loss warning, destination context, save status, and all resolution actions in a bounded accessible dialog.
responsive.compact: Stack change summary and actions. Stay, save-and-continue, and discard remain fully labeled and usable.
responsive.medium: Use a readable dialog width and wrapping actions.
